sub: Named after “those sent forth” (al-mursalāt) in ayah 1
theme: The Day of Judgement is certain. The surah proves it from the winds, history, human birth and the earth, then shows the deniers’ fate and the righteous’ reward, with a refrain of woe to the deniers.
story: Revealed early in Makkah. The Prophet ﷺ received it in a cave at Minā, with Companions learning it straight from his mouth. A snake leapt out and escaped, and he said: “It was saved from your harm, as you were saved from its harm.”

The people of Makkah kept daring him to bring on the Resurrection he warned them about. The surah answers with oaths, signs and scenes: the Day has a fixed time, and when it comes it will overwhelm those who mocked it.
Its refrain, “Woe, that Day, to the deniers,” comes ten times. It was the last surah one Companion heard the Prophet ﷺ recite, in the Maghrib prayer.

sections.title: Oaths by the winds: the promised Day of Sorting Out will come
sections.meaning: Allah swears by winds sent in succession, storm winds and winds that spread clouds, and by angels bringing revelation that separates truth from falsehood. What you are promised will happen. Stars go dark, the sky splits, mountains blow away, the messengers gather: it is the Day of Sorting Out.
points: By the winds: in succession, storming, spreading
By the angels bringing revelation: to excuse or to warn
What you are promised will happen
Stars dimmed, sky split, mountains blown away, messengers gathered
Delayed for the Day of Sorting Out; woe to the deniers
sections.matters: It gives the surah’s core message in one line, ayah 7, and answers those who demanded the Day right now: it has a fixed time, and when it arrives the whole universe comes apart.
sections.story: The people of Makkah kept demanding that the Resurrection be brought on at once. These ayat answer: it is not something to summon on demand. It has a set time, and then everyone will be judged.
explained: The surah opens with five oaths. The first three are most likely winds: sent one after another, blowing violently, spreading clouds and rain. The last two are angels bringing down dhikr, the revelation that separates right from wrong, cutting off excuses and warning. Others take all five as angels.

The answer to the oaths: innamā tūʿadūna la-wāqiʿ, what you are promised will happen. Then the scene: the stars lose their light, the sky splits, the mountains are blasted away, and the messengers arrive at their appointed time to testify. Delayed until when? Yawm al-faṣl, the Day of Sorting Out.
teaches: The Day of Judgement is certain, whatever people say.
The Lord who drives the winds can bring the Day.
Revelation leaves no one an excuse.
Allah delays the Day; He never breaks His promise.
sections.hook: Five oaths, then the answer in 7. Four “when” lines follow (8–11): stars, sky, mountains, messengers. The section ends on the first of ten refrains: wayl yawmaʾidhin lil-mukadhdhibīn (15).

sections.title: Proofs from destroyed nations, human birth and the earth
sections.meaning: Three proofs, each ending with woe to the deniers. History: earlier deniers were destroyed, and later ones follow. Birth: you came from a weak fluid, kept safe in the womb for a set time and perfectly shaped. The earth: it holds the living and the dead, steadied by mountains, with sweet water.
points: Earlier deniers destroyed; later ones follow; woe
From a weak fluid, kept safe in the womb, shaped; woe
Earth holds living and dead; mountains and sweet water; woe
sections.matters: It answers the denier’s doubt with things he can see: past nations, his own birth and the ground under his feet. Whoever made all of this can bring people back.
sections.story: No specific incident. It continues the answer to Makkah’s deniers, pointing them to the fate of earlier nations who rejected their messengers.
explained: Did Allah not destroy the earlier nations who denied their messengers, like ʿĀd, Thamūd and Pharaoh? The later deniers follow the same road. That is how He deals with every criminal.

Look at yourself: made from māʾ mahīn, a weak fluid, placed in qarār makīn, the safe womb, for a known time, and shaped with perfect measure. Look at the earth: kifāt, holding the living on its back and the dead inside it, steadied by towering mountains, with sweet water to drink. After all that, woe to whoever still denies.
teaches: The fate of past nations is a warning for today.
You began as a weak drop; bringing you back is easy for Allah.
Even the grave is a mercy that covers the dead.
Every sip of fresh water is a sign to reflect on.
sections.hook: Three questions, each opening with alam (Did We not): nuhlik (16), nakhluqkum (20), najʿal (25). Each proof closes with the same refrain: 19, 24, 28.

sections.title: Deniers driven to smoke-shade and castle-sized sparks, silenced without excuses
sections.meaning: The deniers are told: go to what you denied, a shade of smoke in three columns that gives no cool and no protection. The Fire throws sparks huge as castles, like yellowish camels. They cannot speak or make excuses. All are gathered: if you have a plan, use it.
points: Go to a shade of smoke in three columns, useless against flame
Sparks like castles, like yellowish camels; woe
No speaking, no excuses allowed; woe
All gathered: if you have a plan, use it; woe
sections.matters: Section 2 gave the proofs; this section shows what happens to those who ignored them. Every escape they relied on is taken away: shade, speech, excuses and schemes.
sections.story: No specific incident. It shows Makkah’s deniers the end of the path they chose.
explained: The deniers are driven off: inṭaliqū, go to the thing you called a lie. Hell’s smoke rises and splits into three columns. It looks like shade, but it gives no coolness and does nothing against the flame. The Fire hurls sparks as big as fortresses, like herds of dark yellow camels.

On that Day they are silent. They are not allowed to make excuses, because the proof against them is complete. The Day has stages: at some they speak, at others they cannot. Allah gathers them with all the earlier nations and challenges them: if you have a plot to escape Me, use it. They have none.
teaches: What people deny today, they will be marched to tomorrow.
Nothing in Hell gives relief, not even its shade.
There are no excuses on that Day, so repent now.
sections.hook: Inṭaliqū (go) opens both 29 and 30. Two lines begin hādhā yawm (this is a Day): 35 and 38. The refrain closes 34, 37 and 40, ending the first ruku.

sections.title: The righteous enjoy shade and fruit; deniers eat briefly and won’t bow
sections.meaning: The God-fearing are in real shade, by springs, with any fruit they desire: “Eat and drink with joy for what you did.” The deniers are told: eat and enjoy a little; you are criminals. When told to bow in prayer, they refuse. If they reject this Quran, what will they ever believe?
points: The righteous among shades, springs and fruits they desire
Eat and drink with joy; so We reward the good; woe
Eat and enjoy a little, you criminals; woe
Told to bow, they do not bow; woe
After this Quran, what will they believe?
sections.matters: It sets the reward right beside the punishment, so the choice is plain. It names a practical sign of denial, refusing to bow in prayer, and ends with a question that leaves no other source of guidance.
sections.story: Reportedly ayah 48 refers to the tribe of Thaqīf, who refused to pray because bowing seemed shameful to them. Some reports count it as the one Madinan ayah in this Makkan surah.
explained: The shade here is real: trees and flowing springs, the opposite of the smoke-shade in section 3. The righteous pick any fruit they want and are told: kulū wa-shrabū hanīʾan, eat and drink with nothing to spoil it, because of what you did. This is how Allah rewards al-muḥsinīn.

Then back to the deniers in this world: eat and enjoy yourselves, but only a little, until death, because you are criminals. When they are told irkaʿū, bow in prayer, they refuse. The last question stands: if they will not believe this Quran, what could they ever believe?
teaches: Shade and springs await those who guard against sin.
Worldly enjoyment is short; don’t trade the lasting for it.
Answer the call to prayer; refusing it is a mark of denial.
If the Quran doesn’t move you, nothing will.
sections.hook: Two “eat” commands face each other: kulū wa-shrabū hanīʾan (43) for the righteous, kulū wa tamattaʿū qalīlan (46) for the deniers. The refrain now comes every other ayah: 45, 47, 49.

groups.text: Allah swears by the winds: sent in succession, storming, and spreading the clouds.
And by the angels who bring revelation, separating truth from falsehood, to remove excuses and to warn.
What you are promised will certainly happen.
The stars go dark, the sky splits, the mountains blow away, and the messengers gather at their appointed time.
It was delayed for the Day of Sorting Out, a Day beyond imagining. Woe to the deniers.
Allah destroyed earlier deniers, and later ones follow; that is how He treats criminals. Woe to the deniers.
He made you from a weak fluid, kept it safe in the womb for a set time, and shaped it. Woe to the deniers.
The earth holds the living and the dead, steadied by tall mountains, with sweet water to drink. Woe to the deniers.
The deniers are told: go to a shade of smoke in three columns, with no cool and no protection.
The Fire throws sparks like castles, like yellowish camels. Woe to the deniers.
On that Day they cannot speak and are not allowed to make excuses. Woe to the deniers.
All are gathered for the Day of Sorting Out: if you have a plan, use it. Woe to the deniers.
The God-fearing are among shades, springs and any fruit they desire.
“Eat and drink with joy for what you did.” That is how Allah rewards those who do good. Woe to the deniers.
Deniers, eat and enjoy a little; you are criminals. Woe to the deniers.
Told to bow in prayer, they refuse. Woe to the deniers. After this Quran, what will they believe?

1.explain: Wal-mursalāti ʿurfā: by those sent one after another, like the hairs of a horse’s mane. Most likely the winds; others say angels sent with Allah’s commands, or the messengers.

2.explain: Fal-ʿāṣifāti ʿaṣfā: winds that blow violently and roar. Or angels, rushing to carry out Allah’s commands like a storm.

3.explain: Wan-nāshirāti nashrā: winds that spread clouds across the sky and bring the rain that revives the earth. Or angels spreading what they are ordered to spread.

4.explain: Fal-fāriqāti farqā: either angels bringing revelation that separates truth from falsehood and lawful from forbidden, or the ayat of the Quran themselves, which make that separation.

5.explain: Fal-mulqiyāti dhikrā: angels delivering the dhikr, the reminder, to the prophets, who pass it on to their people.

6.explain: ʿUdhran aw nudhrā: the revelation removes every excuse, so no one has an argument against Allah, and it warns of what lies ahead. For believers, it moves them to seek forgiveness.

7.explain: This is what all the oaths confirm. Innamā tūʿadūn: the resurrection, reckoning and reward you were promised. La-wāqiʿ: it will certainly happen, beyond any doubt.

8.explain: Ṭumisat: the stars’ light is wiped out, or they scatter from their places. The whole world is plunged into darkness.

9.explain: Furijat: the sky is split open, its sides give way and its edges weaken.

10.explain: Nusifat: the mountains are torn from their places and blown away like dust, leaving the earth a flat plain.

11.explain: Uqqitat: the messengers are gathered at their appointed time, to testify that they delivered the message to their nations.

12.explain: For what Day was all this delayed? The question is asked to show how huge that Day is.

13.explain: Yawm al-faṣl: the Day of Sorting Out, when Allah judges between all creation and settles every account.

14.explain: “What will make you know…?” stresses that the Day is greater than anyone can imagine.

15.explain: The first refrain. Wayl: ruin and destruction; it is also reported to be a valley in Hell. Allah told them and swore to them, and still they denied.

16.explain: Alam nuhlik al-awwalīn: did We not destroy the earlier nations who denied their messengers, like ʿĀd, Thamūd, the people of Lūṭ and Pharaoh?

17.explain: Then We make the later deniers follow them, such as Makkah’s disbelievers. One view: this came true when Makkah’s most stubborn leaders fell at Badr.

18.explain: Kadhālika: this is Allah’s unchanging way with every mujrim, every criminal, past and future. So why not learn from what you see and hear?

19.explain: The second woe: for those who saw clear signs and the fate of earlier nations, and still denied.

20.explain: Māʾ mahīn: a weak, lowly fluid. The One who made you from that can surely make you again.

21.explain: Qarār makīn: a firm, secure resting place, the womb, where it settles and grows.

22.explain: Ilā qadarin maʿlūm: for a known, fixed term, until the time of birth.

23.explain: Fa-qadarnā: We shaped it stage by stage, from drop to clot to lump to a body with a soul (or: We had the power to). Fa-niʿma al-qādirūn: how excellent We are at it.

24.explain: The third woe: for those shown their own creation as a sign, who still deny that their Creator can bring them back.

25.explain: Kifāt: a container that gathers and holds. Allah made the earth hold all people together.

26.explain: Aḥyāʾ on its surface, in their homes; amwāt inside it, in their graves. Graves too are a mercy, covering the dead.

27.explain: Rawāsiya shāmikhāt: tall, firm mountains that keep the earth steady. Māʾ furāt: sweet, fresh water, from the clouds or from springs.

28.explain: The fourth woe: for those who see these blessings, which only Allah provides, and answer them with denial.

29.explain: Inṭaliqū: “Go!” On the Day of Judgement they are told to go to the punishment they used to call a lie.

30.explain: A ẓill, a shade, made of Hell’s smoke. As it rises it splits into thalāth shuʿab, three columns, because it is so vast.

31.explain: Lā ẓalīl: it gives no cool shade and no rest, and does nothing to block the flame, which surrounds them on every side.

32.explain: It hurls sparks like al-qaṣr: huge buildings or fortresses. Another view: like great logs of cut timber.

33.explain: Jimālātun ṣufr: yellowish camels. The Arabs called black camels ṣufr, because their black has a yellow tinge, so the sparks may be dark. Another view: thick ship ropes.

34.explain: The fifth woe: the Fire they called a lie is now right in front of them.

35.explain: Hādhā yawmu lā yanṭiqūn: a Day they cannot speak, out of sheer fear. Other ayat show them speaking: the Day has stages, silent in some and arguing in others.

36.explain: They are not permitted to offer excuses, and no excuse would help. The proof against them is already complete.

37.explain: The sixth woe: those who talked endlessly in this world have no words left.

38.explain: Yawm al-faṣl again: Allah gathers these deniers together with the earlier nations, to judge between everyone.

39.explain: Fa-kīdūn: if you have a trick to escape My hold, use it. A stern challenge: they have no power at all.

40.explain: The seventh woe: on that Day every scheme collapses, and the wrongdoers surrender to the punishment.

41.explain: Al-muttaqūn: those who guarded against sin, doing what was required and avoiding what was forbidden. They are in real shade, from thick trees, beside flowing springs.

42.explain: Fruits of whatever they desire. In this world people eat what they can find; there, they eat whatever they wish.

43.explain: They are told: kulū wa-shrabū hanīʾan, eat and drink with pure enjoyment, nothing spoiling it and no fear of it ending, because of what you did.

44.explain: Innā kadhālika: this is exactly how Allah rewards al-muḥsinīn, those who did well in worship and toward people.

45.explain: The eighth woe: even if losing this bliss were their only punishment, it would be loss enough.

46.explain: Addressed to the deniers in this world: kulū wa tamattaʿū qalīlan, enjoy yourselves a short while, until death. A threat, not permission: you are mujrimūn.

47.explain: The ninth woe: the pleasures will end, and the consequences will remain.

48.explain: Irkaʿū: bow. Either pray, or submit to Allah’s commands; they refuse out of arrogance. Another view: this is said on the Day of Judgement, when they are unable to prostrate.
48.why: Reportedly about the tribe of Thaqīf. Told to accept Islam and pray, they said: “We will not bow; it shames us.” The Prophet ﷺ replied: “There is no good in a religion without bowing and prostration.”

49.explain: The tenth and last woe: those who deny the Quran shut the doors of good on themselves.

50.explain: Fa-bi-ayyi ḥadīthin baʿdahu: if not this Quran, what will they believe? A narration teaches saying “I believe in Allah” after it, outside the obligatory prayers.
